subject: Biotechnology
title: Speed Breeding
description: A fast breakdown of Speed Breeding for builders.

hook.text: Normal wheat breeding takes six generations per year — speed breeding achieves six in a single year.

buildup.text: Extended photoperiod with 22 hours of light accelerates flowering — plants mature in weeks instead of months.

discovery.text: Combined with marker-assisted selection, speed breeding creates improved varieties in 2 to 3 years, not 10 to 15.

twist.text: Speed breeding works for wheat, barley, peas, and canola — but not all crops respond to extended light.

climax.text: CGIAR centers use speed breeding to develop climate-resilient varieties for developing countries — urgency meets innovation.

punchline.text: More light, more generations — speed breeding races against climate change.

quiz.question: How does speed breeding accelerate crop development?
options: It uses CRISPR to skip generations in the breeding process
Extended photoperiod with near-continuous light forces plants to flower and mature faster
It crosses crops with wild species that reproduce more quickly

details.summary: Speed breeding uses extended photoperiods and controlled environments to accelerate plant growth cycles, producing up to six generations per year instead of one or two. Combined with genomic selection, it dramatically compresses the time needed to develop new crop varieties.
details.whyItMatters: Traditional crop breeding takes 10 to 15 years per variety. Speed breeding cuts this to 3 to 5 years, enabling faster responses to emerging diseases, climate changes, and shifting nutritional needs in the global food supply.
takeaways: Extended light periods accelerate flowering and seed production in crops
Up to six generations per year are possible for wheat, barley, and canola
Combining speed breeding with genomics enables rapid trait stacking

faq.question: How does extended light speed up plant breeding?
faq.answer: Many crops flower faster under longer day lengths. Speed breeding provides 22 hours of light daily in growth chambers, pushing plants to flower and set seed in weeks instead of months. Temperature and nutrition are also optimized for rapid cycling.

faq.question: Which crops benefit most from speed breeding?
faq.answer: Long-day crops like wheat, barley, canola, and chickpea respond best. Tropical crops with different photoperiod requirements need modified protocols. Speed breeding has been demonstrated in over 100 crop species and is actively used in breeding programs globally.
